It sets itself apart from sibling methods by explicitly leveraging perceptual or statistical channel importance to prioritize wavelet coefficients during compression, rather than treating all color channels equally [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the method transforms RGB data into an optimized colorspace to assign significance weights based on 'color channel importance' (I) and 'wavelet energy' (E). It provides specific examples of this prioritization, such as assigning different factors to Y, I, and Q channels in YIQ space (4, 1.5, 0.6) and using eigenvalues in PCA to determine eigenvector significance. This directly supports the claim that the method leverages perceptual or statistical channel importance to prioritize coefficients rather than treating all channels equally.
